newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MACDONALD THROWS SIX NO-HIT INNINGS, BREWERS BEAT O'S.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MACDONALD THROWS SIX NO-HIT INNINGS, BREWERS BEAT O'S.

text.p: Ben McDonald pitched six no-hit innings before leaving with a stiff throwing shoulder and former Oriole Jack Voigt hit a solo homer in the fourth as the Milwaukee Brewers defeated Baltimore 3-1 Friday.
McDonald (8-6) threw just 62 pitches. He struck out four and his only blemish came when he hit B.J. Surhoff with a pitch in the second inning. He went to three-ball counts on just two batters.
"He said he could go another inning, but I didn't want to chance it," said Brewers manager Phil Garner.
"I hated more than anybody to come out," admitted McDonald. "It's not about one game or start. I'm a little disappointed, but I look at it as part of the maturity process. There'll be other times."
Mike Fetters, Ron Villone and Doug Jones pitched the final three innings, with Jones striking out two in the ninth for his 21st save. Milwaukee has won three straight after a five-game losing streak.

Jimmy Key (12-5) was reached for three runs and six hits. He has lost four of his last five starts despite allowing more than three runs in just one of them. The Orioles tied a season high with their fourth loss after a five-game winning streak.
Rafael Palmeiro ended the Brewers' no-hit bid in the seventh with a one-out single.

In New York, Andy Pettitte allowed six hits over seven innings and Bernie Williams and Paul O'Neill had RBI singles as the Yankees remained unbeaten against the Detroit Tigers this season (5-0) with a 3-0 victory.
Tino Martinez added a solo homer, his 30th, putting him one behind Oakland's Mark McGwire for the league lead.
Pettitte (10-5), who has not yielded a run in his last 22 innings, struck out four and walked one. Pettitte's scoreless inning streak is the longest since Key tossed 23 from April 5-21, 1993.
Mariano Rivera worked the ninth for his league-leading 28th save.
Brian Moehler (6-7) lost for the first time in five starts.
In Kansas City, Frank Thomas, Ray Durham and Harold Baines homered as the Chicago White Sox posted their fifth straight win while handing the Royals their 10th consecutive loss, 6-2.
The losing streak matches the second-longest in Royals' history. The franchise record is 11, set in 1986.
Wilson Alvarez (8-6) extended his personal win streak to five games, scattering seven hits over seven innings.
Jose Rosado (7-5), the All-Star Game winner, surrendered five earned runs in 6 2/3 innings for the Royals.
Thomas's three-run blast was estimated at 427 feet (130 metres).

In Seattle, Russ Davis's single with one out in the bottom of the ninth off Xavier Hernandez (0-3) scored Rich Amaral with the winning run as the Mariners blew a four-run lead in the top of the inning but beat the Texas Rangers 8-7.
Davis went 3-for-5 with a two-run homer and matched a career high with four RBI.
Bobby Ayala (6-2) got the win despite allowing a bases-loaded walk to Mark McLemore and the tying two-run single to Rusty Greer in the top of the ninth.
Dan Wilson hit a two-run homer and Jose Cruz Jr had a solo shot for Seattle, which has won seven of eight meetings with the Rangers this season.
Dean Palmer hit a solo homer for the Rangers, who have dropped three straight.

In Boston, Pat Hentgen got his major league-leading eighth complete game and Carlos Delgado hit a three-run homer and tied a career-high with five RBI as the Toronto Blue Jays beat the Red Sox for the first time in five tries this season, 8-4.
Hentgen (9-6), last year's Cy Young Award winner, scattered 11 hits and won for the first time in four starts.
John Wasdin (3-4) surrendered four runs -- one earned -- in 1-1/3 innings of relief.

In Minnesota, emergency starter Jason Jacome allowed one run over five innings to earn his first win since 1995 and Marquis Grissom and Julio Franco ended long homerless droughts to lead the Cleveland Indians to a 5-1 victory over the Twins.
Jacome (1-0) started in place of Brian Anderson, who was scratched due to stiffness in his left shoulder. Jose Mesa worked three scoreless innings. Paul Assenmacher struck out one in a perfect ninth.
Grissom hit a two-run homer off Rich Robertson (7-7), his first since May 7. Franco added a solo shot, his first since May 6, for the Indians, who have won six of their last eight.
In Oakland, Garret Anderson drove in three runs and Tony Phillips belted a three-run homer as the Anaheim Angels posted their ninth straight victory over the Athletics, 14-4.
Tim Salmon added three hits and Jim Leyritz knocked in two runs for the Angels, who have won all eight meetings with the Athletics this season, scoring 64 runs.
Jason Dickson (9-4) won for the first time in five starts. Steve Karsay (2-9) yielded five runs in the first inning.
